summary.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q1 FY27: Domino's LFL 2.5% on high base; Popeyes LFL cited at ~45%, EBITDA margin target of 200 bps reiterated.
summary.overview: Management described Popeyes as a second growth engine, with LFL growth of 40-45% attributed to product quality, flavour innovation and store execution. Domino's delivered 2.5% LFL in Q1 FY27 against 11.6% in the prior-year quarter, and management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1. Cost pressure rose: LPG, cheese, oil, labour code and minimum wage hikes were partly offset by pricing and efficiencies, leaving the net margin headwind at about 20 bps QoQ. Management held FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore and the 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with about 100 bps viewed as ahead of track.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin (consolidated, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.6% in Q1 FY26; 0.5% in Q4 FY26
Vs ~70-80 bps remaining headwind flagged last quarter after ~110 bps of pricing already taken

segments.name: Domino's
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 LFL 2.5% on a high base; delivery order volumes not impacted by price increases per management. Minimum order value cut to INR 99 (from INR 149 free-delivery threshold) to match aggregators, lowering average order value.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: LFL growth 40-45%; about 90 stores, with 7 cities above INR 100K ADS for the full quarter. Target ADS is above INR 100K; gross margin still scaling and marketing spend high (about INR 100 crore revenue base invested to reach INR 1,000 crore).

segments.name: Dine-in / takeaway channel
segments.commentary: Dedicated channel team and regional structure built; 2,500 neighbourhood stores; early reversal of trend seen on Wednesdays via Best Deals Ever Wednesday offer. Goal is to hold LFL flat in this channel.

guidance_outlook: Domino's LFL to reach 5-7% for rest of FY27 as bases correct; Q2 FY27 expected better than Q1 FY27 (2.5%).
EBITDA margin expansion target of 200 bps retained (roughly half from Domino's, half from emerging brands); ~100 bps from Popeyes viewed as ahead of track.
FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore maintained; capex increasingly tilted to new Domino's and Popeyes stores, dine-in store investment and technology; supply chain capex materially down.
Management will take calibrated price increases if input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour) persists; commodities described as still in flux.
Expects positive free cash flow for the company over time; tracks ROCE and EPS as primary capital allocation metrics.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance INR 750-900 crore, in line with the previous two years; quarterly capex not disclosed.
Mumbai food factory commissioned in March; some commissioning still pending.
Supply chain investments described as past peak; new commissaries are lowering supply chain costs.
Capex mix: new store expansion (Domino's and Popeyes), existing store upgrades (dine-in), and technology.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 140 bps overall in the quarter per analyst; management said price hikes were 1.5-2% and delivery order volumes were not impacted.
Minimum order value on delivery reduced to INR 99 (and INR 49 on some aggregator platforms) to match aggregators; lower AOV and higher cost per order.
Management said demand is not the constraint; growth is increasingly a question of profitable delivery.
Popeyes competes with fried chicken incumbents; ADS still behind the number one player in the market.
Management declined to disclose AOV; said chicken AOV is higher than pizza and Popeyes can become the highest AOV brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Popeyes LFL acceleration from 9.2% to 45%, and where does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited superior product (marination, fresh chicken, intact pieces), six chicken wing flavours and bun focus, and better store execution with strong openings over the last 3-4 quarters. It declined to forecast normalisation, saying 45% is not a target to hold forever.

qa_highlights.question: Why has per-store employee cost not risen despite minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged per-store headwinds from minimum wages and new stores; productivity gains (orders per labour hour) offset some of the cost, though labour rate per hour has risen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dine-in strategy and expected outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: A dedicated dine-in channel team, store segmentation into dine-in clusters, mall, campus and delivery-first stores, service audits, and offers (Wednesday deals, payment and aggregator partnerships). Early Wednesday results show reversal of trend; first goal is to hold dine-in and takeaway LFL flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can LFL reach 5-7% for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing a two-quarter average of 2.5% (Q1 FY27) and 11.6% (Q1 FY26), which gives over 7%. It said Q2 FY27 will be better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company maximise free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exits from Hong's and Dunkin' and the supply chain build-out now past peak. Capex is shifting to revenue-generating store investment; the internal focus is ROCE and EPS rather than FCF alone. FCF was positive in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is the EBITDA margin target progressing given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 bps of the 200 bps is ahead of track from Popeyes. Domino's is on track, with price increases and supply chain efficiency offsetting LPG, cheese, oil and labour costs. Management said a quarter ago LPG alone cost about 120 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to Domino's margins QoQ after the MOV cut and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost headwinds were about 200 bps against about 100-110 bps of pricing already taken, leaving 70-80 bps. Further pricing, waste reduction and efficiencies cut the net headwind to about 20 bps in the quarter.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour code, minimum wages in about 14-15 states) could widen margin headwind; commodities described as still in flux.
Domino's LFL needs to hold 5-7% on a lower base in H2; Q3 and Q4 face tougher base comparisons.
Delivery volume and MAU-to-MTU conversion softness after price increases; lower AOV from the INR 99 minimum order value.
Popeyes EBITDA breakeven still pending; marketing costs high at current revenue scale; gross margin still scaling at about 90 stores.
Dine-in traffic recovery is early; results so far limited to Wednesdays.
key_quotes: So these 3 structural tailwinds or structural factors are giving us 40%-45% growth rate.
But we do believe this 100 basis point is ahead of the track.
And if you're not able to kind of manage the shape of the P&L, we will take calibrated price increase.
So I think commodities are still in a flux.
We don't actually declare delivery percentage for Popeyes.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on Popeyes momentum, the Domino's 5-7% LFL path and the 200 bps margin target, with about 100 bps described as ahead of track. It was cautious on input costs, saying commodities remain in flux and price increases will be calibrated, and it declined to share AOV or Popeyes delivery mix and to forecast Popeyes LFL normalisation.

adds.what: FY27 growth capex INR 750-900 crore (new Domino's and Popeyes stores, dine-in upgrades, technology); guidance held, quarterly split not disclosed
Mumbai food factory, commissioning still pending

growth.why: Domino's LFL guided to 5-7% for the rest of FY27 after 2.5% in Q1 on a high base, Popeyes LFL ~40-45% with ~90 stores, and FY27 capex held at INR 750-900 crore for new stores, but no revenue growth figure was given and the Domino's LFL recovery is not yet proven.
